all_144.q1: Most complaints are about ordinary photos (80/144); screenshots and documents are rare in public posts (10/144). Only 15/144 texts mention the photo being old (keyword match), so public posts can't yet say which old photos fail.
all_144.q2: Approximate time is the most-kept cue (40/144); 47/144 keep no searchable cue at all.
all_144.q3_lead: The date is the most-lost detail (37/144), then album (29/144).

brief_population.q1: Most complaints are about ordinary photos (28/45); screenshots and documents are rare in public posts (1/45). Only 7/45 texts mention the photo being old (keyword match), so public posts can't yet say which old photos fail.
brief_population.q2: Approximate time is the most-kept cue (19/45); every attempt in this group keeps at least one cue.
brief_population.q3_lead: The date is the most-lost detail (33/45), then exact words (9/45).

headlines.q3_note: Among the cues the brief covers, text inside the photo has the highest not-found rate when it is remembered (5 of 8 known outcomes; small n).
headlines.q4: 20 of 32 quoted queries are a single word and 9 are two words: people reduce a rich memory to one noun ('dog', 'cake', 'restaurant'). Only 3 are full sentences: 2 found the photo, 1 did not, and only 1 is explicitly an Ask Photos query.

verdict.rule: If top-2 sets differ, interviews break the tie (Plan 2, section 3).
